sources.entry: jmc - jmc is new macOS media organizer.

summary.one_liner: jmc is a media manager and player for macOS, written in Swift, aimed at being a drop-in replacement for Music.app with a cleaner interface.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes jmc as a macOS media manager and player meant to be a drop-in replacement for Music.app, with a consistent interface and keyboard controls. It offers library organization tools that track album artwork, PDFs, logs, cue sheets and other files, and can organize added files by moving or copying them or leave them untouched. A Location Manager tracks where files live so lost files can be relocated, and external volumes are shown in the sidebar with their music filtered by availability. Advanced Search filters the library by arbitrary criteria and builds smart playlists. Shared Libraries lets jmc clients on nearby machines connect over Ethernet, Wi-Fi, or peer-to-peer Wi-Fi to stream music or drag and drop media. It can also import an existing iTunes Library.xml file.
use_cases: managing a large local music library on macOS
replacing Music.app with a simpler player
organizing album artwork, PDFs and cue sheets
relocating music files moved between external drives
building smart playlists with advanced search
streaming or transferring music between Macs on a LAN
importing an iTunes library into a new player
how_to_run: Download the latest stable build from the releases link in the README, or
Clone the repository and compile jmc from source manually in Xcode
Run the app and, in the File menu, choose "Import iTunes Library" and select your iTunes Library.xml file (optional)
notable: Drop-in replacement for Music.app with a focus on responsive UI with large libraries
Location Manager to relocate files after they move between volumes or libraries
Shared Libraries: stream and transfer media between jmc clients over Ethernet, Wi-Fi or peer-to-peer Wi-Fi
Integrates with Apple Music and iCloud Music Library, per the README overview
caveats: Built from source requires compiling Swift code manually; the README gives no build steps beyond that
